correctness.rationale: For the fixed point p, p_{2r}=0 and p_{2r+1}=1-p_r; hence ones lie at one position parity and zero runs have maximum length three. For a factor of odd length containing a one, all internal cyclic gaps between ones are odd; the unique boundary cyclic zero gap is even. Any represented rotation must cut inside that same even gap. At most three splittings of an even gap have both leading and trailing zero runs <=3. All-zero factors contribute one rotation. The explicit B=mu^{2j}(0), j>=1, begins 01, ends 00, and BB occurs; B0, 0B and 00B[:-1] are three distinct represented rotations. Aperiodicity follows from p_i=v2(i+1) modulo 2 and establishes the Morse-Hedlund lower bound. The extracted standalone finite checker passed at odd lengths <=129 and five infinite-family representatives; the proof, not the finite test, establishes the quantifiers.

value.rationale: This infinite-language structural bound supplies a sharp uniform ceiling on represented rotation-class cardinality at every odd length, attained at infinitely many nontrivial lengths. It yields linear cyclic-complexity growth along all odd lengths despite constant values at every dyadic length. The parity-sensitive oscillation addresses the shape of a classical invariant beyond numerical dyadic class counts and is not an arbitrary finite cutoff.
